components.name: Pace Line
components.description: The signature: the plan dashed, spending solid, today as the sun.

narrative.overview: Finances inherits life-dashboard's Clay x Japandi world instead of inventing its own, so the two apps read as one system. It answers "are we on track?" with one line, spending against plan across the financial month, and keeps everything else quiet. Phone first (390 px), both themes always; only the tokens change between them.
keyCharacteristics: Washi by day, charcoal by night. Raised means you can press it or it holds things; pressed in means a well or the current choice.
Serif italic headlines, gothic body, mono uppercase labels.
The pace line is the signature: dashed plan, solid spending, today as the sun.

rules.name: The Upstream Rule
rules.body: Tokens in `base.css` are copied from `life-dashboard/frontend/src/styles/base.css` on purpose and life-dashboard's DESIGN.md is their authority: change a token in life-dashboard first, then here. Finance's own additions are only `--quiet`, `--fill`, `--tick`, `--tap` and the `--series-*` colours. Copied tokens finance doesn't use yet stay as copied.

rules.name: The One Vermilion Rule
rules.body: One vermilion mark per view: the sun or the primary action. When a later step's action appears, the earlier button goes plain. The current-tab underline, focus ring, caret and link hover are wayfinding and don't count.

rules.name: The Quiet Rule
rules.body: `--muted` is only for mono labels, graphic marks and disabled controls. Small sans text uses `--quiet` (4.5:1 on every surface, both themes).

rules.name: The Series Rule
rules.body: The `--series-*` colours are derived in `trends.css` and validated for colour-blind separation on the card in both themes. They are not free choices: re-run the validator before changing one. They belong to Trends; Month's meters stay `--fill`.

rules.name: The Typewriter Rule
rules.body: Never change the mono labels' font or greys; life-dashboard holds that decision.

rules.name: The Position Rule
rules.body: Phone tables are position-based: each cell is placed by its column number (`transactions.css`, `setup.css`, `import.css`). Adding, removing or moving a column means changing the phone grid in the same edit, or the cells land in the wrong places.

rules.name: The Soft Clay Rule
rules.body: Everything you can press sinks at `--press-in` and puffs back at `--press-out`, darkening to `--press-tint`; `press.ts` holds a press at least 120 ms so a quick tap still shows it. Reduced motion turns it off.

rules.name: The Sun and Moon Rule
rules.body: Today's dot is a raised vermilion sun by day and a hollow gold moon by night, and hollow in both themes whenever spending doesn't reach today.

rules.name: The No Guessing Rule
rules.body: Month never guesses after a gap. With status `gap` or `empty` it says so ("Can't tell yet", "No bank files yet"), shows no meters or today tick, folds the plan away, and offers the import as the one vermilion button.

dos: Do take the current financial month from the pace endpoint's `current_month`, never the calendar.
Do use plain CSS classes in `src/styles/`, with inline `style` only for computed values such as a width or position.
Do write plain words in British spelling, neutral about which of the two people is reading.
Do say spent with "more than planned", always: "Spent €133 more than planned by now."
Do check both themes at 390 px and on a desktop.
donts: Don't add a literal colour, radius or shadow where a token exists.
Don't make a flat bordered box; only a disabled chip is flat, with a hairline.
Don't add indigo, glass, or decorative gradients and glows; the night lamplight behind the page is inherited and the only one.
